result.instructions: Tools for FieldPulse, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "List the jobs created this week with their status and who is assigned to them."; "Show the details and the balance due of invoice 1234."; "Create a customer lead for Maria Lopez, phone 555-0142, with a service address on Oak Street.". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes FieldPulse data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run fieldpulse_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run fieldpulse_request_feature to record the request. Paid plan: Pro (unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month), $9/month or $90/year). Pro can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run fieldpulse_upgrade (plan "monthly" or "yearly"); it returns a payment link for the user to open. fieldpulse_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: fieldpulse_create_customer
tools.title: Create customer
tools.description: WRITE: create a customer (lead or account). Give first_name and/or last_name, or a unique display_name. Creates a new record every call; check fieldpulse_list_customers first to avoid duplicates. POST /customers.

display_name.description: Required by FieldPulse when first and last name are empty; must be unique.

assigned_to.description: User id the customer is assigned to (see fieldpulse_list_users); null clears it.

tools.name: fieldpulse_update_customer
tools.title: Update customer
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of one customer (only the fields you pass). If FieldPulse asks for a name, include first_name/last_name or display_name. PUT /customers/{customerId}.

display_name.description: Required by FieldPulse when first and last name are empty; must be unique.

assigned_to.description: User id the customer is assigned to (see fieldpulse_list_users); null clears it.

tools.name: fieldpulse_create_job
tools.title: Create job
tools.description: WRITE: create a job for an existing customer. Needs customer_id, job_type and the numeric billing value FieldPulse requires; set a status (1-6) or a custom status_id + status_workflow_id. Creates a new job every call. POST /jobs.

job_type.description: Job type label, e.g. the service name.

billing.description: The integer billing value FieldPulse requires for a job.

status.description: 1 = new, 2 = in progress, 3 = pending, 4 = completed, 5 = canceled, 6 = on the way.

status_id.description: A custom status id (see fieldpulse_list_job_workflow_statuses); needs status_workflow_id.

status_workflow_id.description: The status workflow of status_id (see fieldpulse_list_job_status_workflows).

start_time.description: Start, yyyy-mm-dd or ISO 8601 with a timezone.

end_time.description: End, yyyy-mm-dd or ISO 8601 with a timezone.

due_date.description: Due date, yyyy-mm-dd or ISO 8601 with a timezone.

location_id.description: A location of the customer (see fieldpulse_list_locations).

assignments.description: Who the job is assigned to.

tools.name: fieldpulse_update_job
tools.title: Update job
tools.description: WRITE: change a job: status, schedule, notes, assignments, location. FieldPulse requires customer_id, job_type and billing on every update, so this reads the job first and keeps those (and its current status) unless you pass new values. The read and the write are two requests; FieldPulse offers no version check. PUT /jobs/{jobId}.

status.description: 1 = new, 2 = in progress, 3 = pending, 4 = completed, 5 = canceled, 6 = on the way.

status_id.description: A custom status id (see fieldpulse_list_job_workflow_statuses); needs status_workflow_id.

status_workflow_id.description: The status workflow of status_id (see fieldpulse_list_job_status_workflows).

start_time.description: Start, yyyy-mm-dd or ISO 8601 with a timezone.

end_time.description: End, yyyy-mm-dd or ISO 8601 with a timezone.

due_date.description: Due date, yyyy-mm-dd or ISO 8601 with a timezone.

location_id.description: A location of the customer (see fieldpulse_list_locations).

assignments.description: Who the job is assigned to.
